definition: Dissemination means the act of spreading information or ideas widely to many people.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word dissemination. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know dissemination should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After spotting the comet, the observatory turned at once to the dissemination of its findings: within hours, telegrams carried the coordinates to astronomers on three continents.
An announcement shares news once, with whoever happens to be present; dissemination is a sustained effort to reach many audiences through many channels.
Saturation goes further than dissemination — it floods every available channel until no member of the audience could possibly miss the message.

Circulation is information moving from person to person — a rumor circulates, a memo makes the rounds. Dissemination is more organized and deliberate: someone actively pushes information out through multiple channels to reach many people at once. Circulation can just happen; dissemination is a planned effort.

Propagation is the spreading of ideas or beliefs to an ever-wider audience, and it highlights the growth itself — the idea catching on. Dissemination centers on the sender's organized act of pushing information out widely. Ideas propagate almost on their own; findings are disseminated on purpose, through chosen channels.

Broadcasting sends one message out to many receivers at once, in a single transmission — radio and television are the model. Dissemination is broader and more sustained: many channels, many audiences, over time. One broadcast can be a piece of a dissemination effort, but dissemination names the whole campaign.
